[P3] Qualify the completion guarantee for abandoned steps

If the handler returns immediately after an early-completed batch, `withDurableExecution` drains queued checkpoints but does not await abandoned branch promises. The invocation can therefore end while a slow step is still running; its remaining side effects are not guaranteed to happen. Saying the function “finishes it” could lead callers to rely on cleanup or writes that never complete. State that abandoned work may continue while the invocation remains active, but is not guaranteed to finish or reach its next checkpoint. Apply the same qualification to the new `BatchItemStatus.STARTED` comment.
